title: Scan three items with a handheld barcode scanner, turning the one whose code faces away, and bag them
instruction: Scan the shopping and put it in the bagging area.
context: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics counts 3,106,300 cashier jobs (2025, Occupational Outlook Handbook) and lists 'Scan customers' purchases' and 'Bag or wrap customers' purchases' among what cashiers typically do: this is the core of the job. The skill is physical. The scanner is a tool held by its grip whose window has to be aimed at a small target at the right distance and angle, with nothing in between; a code that faces the wrong way has to be found and the item turned with the other hand; and each item has to be read exactly once, because an unread item in the bag is stock leaving unpaid and a second read charges the customer twice. Here three items stand on a checkout counter: a tin of beans, a carton of crackers and a juice carton. The crackers' barcode faces the robot, the juice's faces its right front, and the tin's faces away. A cordless handheld scanner stands in its cradle, a bagging tray is at one side and a customer display has one lamp per item.
setup: Counter top is z = 0.7475 m; positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left. All real size; shapes are CAD models. (1) Cordless handheld barcode scanner, free, 180 g: pistol grip 34 x 30 mm in section and 112 mm tall, head 100 mm long, 160 mm tall overall; its red scan window (48 x 26 mm) faces forward and 10 degrees down. It stands on the foot of its grip in (2) its charging cradle, fixed, 96 x 86 x 30 mm, socket 42 x 38 mm and 18 mm deep at (0.33, -0.36), window toward +x. (3) Tin of baked beans, free, 66 mm across, 110 mm tall, 300 g, at (0.375, 0.13); its barcode is centred 85 mm up on the side facing +x, AWAY from the robot; the side toward the robot shows only the product name. (4) Carton of crackers, free, 110 (x) x 55 (y) x 170 mm, 200 g, at (0.40, -0.01); barcode on its narrow face toward the robot (-x), centred 110 mm up. (5) Gable-top juice carton, free, 60 x 60 x 140 mm, 250 g, at (0.47, -0.11), standing turned 70 degrees anticlockwise seen from above; its barcode, centred 90 mm up, faces the robot's right front (direction (-0.34, -0.94)). Each item has ONE barcode: a white patch 45 x 30 mm with black bars, long side level. The crackers' and juice's codes are in the top camera's view at the start; the tin's is not (it shows in the overview picture, taken from the far right). The goods stand on (6) a black rubber counter mat, 220 x 380 x 2 mm, centre (0.435, 0.0). (7) Bagging tray, fixed, 240 (x) x 220 (y) mm outside, rim 22 mm, centre (0.36, 0.29). (8) Customer display on a pole at (0.62, 0.12), fixed, 285 mm tall, turned 50 degrees toward the robot's right, with three lamps captioned BEANS, CRACKERS and JUICE, unlit; a lamp lights green when its item has been read. Real trial: see the README section 'Building the real parts' (any cordless pistol-grip scanner with a stand, set to log each read with its time; three ballasted goods with printed barcode stickers; tape marks).
scoring: Read from measured poses every step. A read of an item registers when the scanner's window is aimed at its barcode: barcode centre 5 to 20 cm from the window centre and within 3 cm of the window's axis line, axis within 30 degrees of the barcode's normal, a clear line of sight (window on the barcode's outward side; the straight line from window to barcode passes through no item's body, its own included), held 0.5 s. One code at a time: the one nearest the axis. A code is read again (a double charge) if the aim has left it for 0.5 s and then holds on it again. An item is in the tray when every corner of its bounding box (the whole item, not its centre) is inside the tray's outline and it is down on the tray's floor or on other goods in it, standing or lying; it is bagged once it is also let go (both grippers at least 3 cm from it). Each item earns 1/3 when it has been read exactly once and is bagged at the end. An item put in the tray unread (0.5 s on its floor, or let go on the goods in it) latches unscanned_in_bag: that item earns nothing and the trial is capped at 0.33, even if it is read afterwards. Every extra read takes 1/3 off (floor 0); the item read twice also earns nothing. An item that leaves the counter, or is dropped, thrown or knocked (it moves faster than 0.5 m/s with no gripper at it), earns nothing. With all three items earned the score is 0.9 until the scanner is put away for 1 s: both grippers at least 8 cm from its grip, and it stands in its cradle or lies on the counter, no part of it over the tray or within 2 cm of an item, never dropped; then 1.0. Taking an item out of the tray and putting it back changes nothing; a read item put back on the counter earns nothing. An item held up to the scanner in its cradle is read by the same rule. Doing nothing scores 0. Reported: reads per item, double reads, items bagged, items dropped, the flag, scanner put down. Real trial: the scanner's log has one line per read (time, code) with its same-code delay set to 0.5 s. Reads per item = lines with that item's code; exactly one line each is required; a second line is a double charge. A read through or from behind an item cannot happen. From the video: the time each item is first set down in the tray or on goods in it; if that is before its log line, the flag is set. An item that falls more than 2 cm out of the gripper or is knocked over earns nothing. From a top photo at the end: each item wholly inside the tray's rim, grippers clear; scanner in its stand or lying on the counter clear of tray and goods.
reset_notes: Fixed starting poses, no randomisation; arms at the ready pose. Real trial: each item is set on its tape outline on the mat (the juice carton's outline is drawn turned 70 degrees; the tin's barcode sticker turned to the far side, checked against an arrow on the mat), the scanner is stood in its stand on its tape outline with the window toward the far side, the tray is taped down, the scanner's log is cleared and one test read of a spare code confirms it is logging.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, rigid. The scanner reads nothing optically: a read is a rule on measured poses (distance, angle, aim, line of sight past the goods' colliders, 0.5 s hold). Grippers, tray and cradle do not block the line; glare, focus and bar orientation are not modelled. Lamps are switched by the rule. Colliders are primitives under CAD visuals: scanner two boxes, cradle a socket 2 to 4 mm wider than drawn, cartons boxes, tin a cylinder, tray a floor and four walls. Labels are thin geometry.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 993 steps (the scanner stayed in its cradle; nothing was read or bagged); termination: task_budget_limit (the runner's cap of 20 requests per task). Scripted demo: 1 after 1,403 steps.
